title: Orsen and the Oath
premise: Kestrel Nakamura, a temple scribe bound by debt to the Order of the Quiet Flame, has survived Thornfell's mountains by knowing every smuggler's road and keeping his head down. But when he transcribes a century-old book of prophecies and finds tonight's date—and his own name—inked by a dead oracle, his invisibility shatters. The prophecy names him bearer of the Ember Vow, an oath that could either seal or reignite the war between the mountain clans and the lowland empire. Hunted by imperial inquisitors, clan zealots, and the temple masters who sold him out, Kestrel must decide whether to destroy the vow, claim it, or pass it on. In the end, he breaks the oath publicly at the moon's thirteenth turn, trading his own freedom to the inquisitors so the secret dies with him—and the war never comes.
about_author: Lior Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing marginalia in monastic libraries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people trapped by paperwork, prophecy, and other people's promises.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A night of copying ledgers in the Quiet Flame temple establishes his crushing debt, his photographic memory for routes, and his careful habit of being forgettable. He smuggles one small letter as a side job to eat. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking a sharp mind.

chapters.title: The Book That Waits
chapters.summary: Kestrel is ordered to recatalogue the sealed archive after an earthquake cracks its vault. Among water-damaged volumes he finds the Oracle of Sable Turn, written 100 years ago. His POV; wonder curdling into dread as he recognizes the binding style of his own temple.

chapters.title: Tonight, By Name
chapters.summary: Reading by candlelight, Kestrel finds a passage dated to this very night naming 'the scribe Nakamura' as bearer of the Ember Vow. He tells himself it's coincidence—until the described omen (a cracked bell) happens outside his window. POV: Kestrel. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: The Master Who Smiles
chapters.summary: Temple master Ilvane summons Kestrel, seemingly kind, probing what he read. Kestrel lies well but notices her hands trembling. Her POV closes the chapter, revealing she has known about the prophecy for years and needs a disposable bearer. Beat: betrayal foreshadowed.

chapters.title: Thirteen Bells
chapters.summary: The cracked bell tolls thirteen times—an impossibility. Imperial inquisitors arrive at the temple gates asking after 'a scribe.' Kestrel flees through the crypt tunnels only he knows. POV alternates Kestrel and inquisitor Captain Sera Voss. Beat: panic sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Roads Only He Knows
chapters.summary: Kestrel escapes into Thornfell using smuggler paths from memory. He encounters Brannoc, a clan courier he once guided, who owes him a favor and becomes reluctant ally. Kestrel's POV. Beat: first warmth—the cost of having no one.

chapters.title: What the Clans Remember
chapters.summary: Brannoc's holdfast. Clan elders recognize the prophecy's sigil tattooed faintly on Kestrel's wrist—a birthmark he never understood. Zealot priestess Maren declares him the Oathbearer and wants to use him immediately. Kestrel's POV. Beat: being seen is worse than being hunted.

chapters.title: The First Price
chapters.summary: Imperial scouts raid the holdfast hunting Kestrel. Brannoc's younger sister dies covering his escape. Kestrel carries the guilt out into the snow. Alternating POVs: Kestrel and Voss, who begins doubting her orders. Beat: survival has a body count already.

chapters.title: Voss Interrogates a Ghost
chapters.summary: Voss's POV chapter. She interrogates Master Ilvane, realizing the temple engineered everything—Kestrel was chosen because he's expendable and because his bloodline traces to the last Oathbreaker. Beat: cold fury; the law she serves is rotten.

chapters.title: The Oracle's Cave
chapters.summary: Following the prophecy's geography, Kestrel and Brannoc find the Sable Oracle's cave, preserved mid-writing. Frescoes show the full vow ritual—and its price: the bearer's name erased from every memory and record. Kestrel's POV. Beat: temptation of oblivion.

chapters.title: Maren's Sermon
chapters.summary: Clan zealots catch up and seize Kestrel, intending to force the vow at the next dark moon to rally the clans to war. Maren's POV reveals she knows the erasure clause and considers it holy martyrdom—for him, not her. Beat: righteous cruelty.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Iron
chapters.summary: Captive in the zealot camp, Kestrel negotiates using his knowledge of imperial supply roads, buying time and planting doubt among pragmatist clansfolk. Brannoc works his own rescue. Kestrel's POV. Beat: cunning rekindled—he is more than a vessel.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Escape during a storm; Brannoc is gravely wounded shielding Kestrel. Hiding in a shrine, Kestrel reads the prophecy's final page, which he'd avoided: it names not just a bearer but a choice, and hints the oracle wrote it under duress. Kestrel's POV. Beat: the map is not the territory.

chapters.title: Ilvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilvane intercepts them, alone, offering sanctuary—and truth: the temple faked parts of the prophecy a generation ago to control the clans, but the original underneath is real and worse. She wants Kestrel to complete the vow to bury her forgery. Ilvane's POV. Beat: villainy with a human face.

chapters.title: The Lowland Road
chapters.summary: Refusing both temple and clans, Kestrel walks into the imperial capital itself to find the oracle's lost second manuscript, believing it contains a way to void the vow rather than fulfill it. Voss finds him—and instead of arresting him, listens. Dual POV. Beat: strange alliance.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Archive
chapters.summary: In the imperial archive they discover the second manuscript—partially burned decades ago on Ilvane's orders. What survives confirms the vow can be unmade, but only publicly, by the bearer, at the thirteenth turn, at cost of the bearer's liberty. Voss's POV. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Zealots at the Gate
chapters.summary: Maren's forces besiege the capital's old quarter, believing Kestrel imprisoned there. Voss must choose between her oath and the truth; she releases Kestrel officially 'escaped.' Brannoc, half-healed, arrives with clan pragmatists ready to hear him out. Multiple POVs. Beat: loyalties realigning.

chapters.title: The Moon's Last Shadow
chapters.summary: Eve of the thirteenth turn. Kestrel drafts, in his scribe's hand, the public unmaking—every forged line named, every true danger stated. He says goodbye to Brannoc, asking him to remember the sister who died, since Kestrel's own name will be erased. Kestrel's POV. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Climax: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: At the ruined bell tower before assembled clans, inquisitors, and temple masters, Kestrel performs the unmaking rite as Maren tries to kill him mid-word and Ilvane tries to discredit him. Voss arrests Ilvane with imperial warrant; Brannoc holds the crowd. Kestrel speaks the vow backward and it unravels. Beat: terrible triumph.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: The vow takes its price: records blur, faces slacken, and the crowd slowly forgets why they came. Only Brannoc, holding the sister's token, and Voss, holding the warrant, retain fragments. Kestrel surrenders to Voss as a nameless prisoner. Alternating POVs. Beat: hollow, necessary sacrifice.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: Voss arranges the lightest lawful sentence—archive labor in a distant lowland town—telling herself it's justice, not kindness. Ilvane falls; Maren's movement fractures without its miracle. Brannoc visits the nameless prisoner and calls him 'friend,' which lands like a name. Voss's POV. Beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: A New Hand Writes
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Kestrel's POV under a new assigned name. Copying mundane ledgers again, he finds a fresh margin note in an unknown hand: a single thirteenth-bell glyph and the word 'remember.' He smiles, chooses not to report it, and keeps writing. Beat: identity survives erasure; the story continues beyond the page.
